title: Outlook for Mac: sensitivity label inheritance from email attachments
summary: The roadmap facts, inheritance behaviour, policy paths and PowerShell settings are supported. The briefing correctly reports Microsoft's conflicting Mac support documentation; minor corrections concern additional citations and checklist controls not represented in the table.

claims.claim: Outlook for Mac can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on attached files' labels.
claims.quote: When composing an email in Outlook for Mac, Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels can be automatically applied or recommended based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.

Learn describes an email label being dynamically selected from sensitivity labels applied to attachments.
claims.quote: With this configuration, a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Only attachment labels published to the user are candidates for inheritance.
claims.quote: based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Outlook selects the highest priority eligible label when it supports inheritance.
claims.quote: The highest priority label is dynamically selected when it's supported by Outlook.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Inheritance does not replace a manually applied email label, including a lower priority manual label.
claims.quote: When an email message has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by label inheritance from email attachments.

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority email label applied automatically or as a default.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label

claims.claim: Inheritance does not override a higher priority email label.
claims.quote: but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Inheritance requires a physical attachment and does not use a SharePoint or OneDrive link as an attachment.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: By default the email receives the automatically selected label's encryption, including Do Not Forward.
claims.quote: By default, if the automatically selected label applies encryption, the same encryption is applied to the email.

claims.claim: If the highest priority label applies only user-defined permissions for Word, PowerPoint and Excel, no label or protection is selected for the email.
claims.quote: no label or protection is selected for the email message because Outlook doesn't support this label configuration.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The Office for Mac release notes list attachment label inheritance in version 16.113.
claims.quote: Version 16.113 (Build 26091433) ... Security: Outlook can automatically inherit an appropriate sensitivity label from labeled attachments

claims.claim: The release notes date version 16.113 to 16 September 2026.
claims.quote:
September 16, 2026

Version 16.113 (Build 26091433)

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn Outlook capabilities table still lists attachment label inheritance as Not available for Mac, contrary to the release notes.
claims.quote: | Label inheritance from email attachments | Current Channel: 2302+  Monthly Enterprise Channel: 2302+  Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel: 2302+ | Not available | Not available | Not available | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: An inherited label must be scoped to both files and emails; a label scoped to only one cannot be inherited.
claims.quote:
Label inheritance from email attachments:

- For this configuration, the label must be scoped to both files and emails.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Without the recommend option, Outlook applies the inherited label automatically rather than asking the user to apply it.
claims.quote: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it. Without this selection, the label is automatically applied

claims.claim: The recommendation option becomes selectable after selecting the inheritance checkbox.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can remove an automatically inherited label or choose another label before sending.
claims.quote: users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: The inheritance settings reside in a label policy and apply to the users and groups selected for that policy.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Inheritance is admin-opt-in through a sensitivity label policy setting.
claims.quote: Turn on email inheritance ... You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy ... select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: The Purview path through Publishing policies, policy, Edit Policy and Default settings for emails reaches Email inherits highest priority label from attachments under Inherit label from attachments.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. For the section Inherit label from attachments, select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} enables automatic attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user. Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}

claims.claim: The Purview path through Publishing policies, policy, Edit Policy and Default settings for emails reaches Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it under Inherit label from attachments.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} configures a recommendation prompt instead of automatic inheritance.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy opens the Create policy configuration for an existing policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane ... This action starts the Create policy configuration

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Office apps require a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: Outlook for Mac supports sensitivity labels for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Mac, sensitivity labels are supported for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.

claims.claim: Learn lists Information Protection role groups, including Information Protection Admins, for creating and configuring labels and label policies.
claims.quote: You can use the following role groups: ... Information Protection Admins ... These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies.

claims.claim: A custom role group with the Sensitivity Label Administrator role can manage labels and label policies.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are alternative permissions routes.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Licensing is included in qualifying sensitivity-label subscriptions, with feature-level entitlement uncertainty stated in the notes.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The service description says sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Manual Sensitivity Labeling row includes Microsoft 365 E5, A5, G5, E3, A3, G3, F1, F3 and Business Premium.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F1/F3/Business Premium ... Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included

claims.claim: Both administrators managing Information Protection and end users using it need appropriate licenses.
claims.quote: the administrator creating and managing Information Protection features must have the appropriate licenses ... Similarly, end users also need the appropriate licenses to use the functionality in their respective client applications.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The service description contains no separate feature row for email attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: service description text for inherit and attachment; read its Information Protection feature tables. Its inheritance row concerns Microsoft 365 Copilot input-to-output inheritance, not Outlook attachment inheritance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A specific licensing distinction between manual-label and automatic-label entitlements for attachment inheritance is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: label inheritance email attachments licensing E3 E5 sensitivity label AttachmentAction. Read Manage sensitivity labels, Set-LabelPolicy and the Purview service description; no passage assigns this policy option to either entitlement tier.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The service description publishes no separate meter or price for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook label inheritance attachments licensing price meter; service description text for inherit, attachment, price and meter. Read Information Protection licensing tables; no attachment-inheritance price or meter was found.

claims.claim: The roadmap item does not mention licensing.
claims.quote: This helps users consistently protect sensitive information, reduces manual labeling effort, and supports organizational compliance requirements by aligning email protection with the sensitivity of attached content.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated how an already-enabled inheritance policy begins applying to Mac users after their client update.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac label inheritance attachments existing policy update AttachmentAction automatically enabled. Read Office apps inheritance instructions, Outlook capabilities, Set-LabelPolicy and Mac 16.113 release notes; no existing-policy rollout statement found.

claims.claim: Inheritance makes email-label-based mail-flow, DLP and encryption controls operate on the inherited attachment label.
claims.quote: Any mail-flow or DLP related controls that are tied to the email's label ... is applied based on the email's attachments.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/pspf-label-publishing#label-inheritance to sources to support the email-label-based mail-flow and DLP applicability statement.

claims.claim: An inherited label's encryption can prevent recipients not authorized by its permissions from opening the email.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted ... Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels to sources for the statement about recipients being unable to open encrypted email.

claims.claim: Files and emails scopes are set on the sensitivity label rather than the label policy.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, the options selected determine the label's scope for the settings that you can configure and where they'll be visible when they're published

claims.claim: Label priority is a label-level order setting that determines which attachment label wins inheritance.
claims.quote: When you've created all the labels you need, review their order and if necessary, move them up or down. To change the order of a label, select ... for Actions, and then select one of the reordering options, such as Move up or Move down.

claims.claim: Information Protection > Sensitivity labels identifies the label list used to review labels and their scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: Expand the parenthetical route to 'Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels'.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review label publication, label scopes, priority and encryption, but the table contains only inheritance and recommendation settings.
claims.quote: Check which labels are published to Mac users and confirm each is scoped to both files and emails ... Review label priority order ... List the labels that apply encryption
claims.fix: The publication, label-scope, priority and encryption review steps have no corresponding control rows. Remove these checklist bullets from Before rollout; do not add unverified control rows.

claims.claim: Learn documents Windows-specific attachment inheritance outcomes for Double Key Encryption.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.
